scope_note: This is a required-work inventory, not a complete proof specification. Smoke tests do not set these cases to implemented. Professional parity must be scoped explicitly against licensed reference software.

cases.progress: Unix UID/GID/groups, private state and Bash login profiles are tested. A root gateway starts the supervisor with the R account credentials. Windows uses its service account; PAM sessions remain open.

Six Linux checks passed for private Unix sockets, real R HTTP, native WebSocket and SockJS reactivity, shared-secret denial and cleanup. Root-to-user identity checks also pass with sockets. Windows uses loopback TCP.

Seven checks passed for named/custom token formats, streaming completion, escaping, password exclusion, log rotation/reload and bounded-writer loss metrics. dev output intentionally omits terminal colors.
Multiple listeners and virtual-host routing passed actual HTTP checks.
Dynamic nested discovery and real static HTTP integration passed on the candidate.
Unix modes are applied independently of umask; real worker tests pass with service-owned and worker-owned logs. Windows uses inherited directory ACLs.
Unix primary/supplementary group lookup and deny behavior implemented; primary-group and unknown-group cases pass on Linux. Windows rejects unsupported OS group lookup.
Inherited Google tag markup and disabling overrides tested with real Shiny HTTP. Tests do not execute external scripts or contact Google.
Five socket checks passed on Windows and Linux: active requests reset deadlines, idle/incomplete connections close, and zero disables expiration. TLS/ACME and browser transport regressions pass.
Gzip/deflate negotiation, disabled mode, range responses and small bodies passed six live HTTP checks; seven SockJS browser modes pass with compression enabled.
Opt-in .shiny_app.conf parsing and generation tracking implemented; full upstream override scope remains under review.

Eight checks passed for inherited directory/status-error templates, Handlebars escaping, file reload, specific fallback, invalid syntax and protected static files. Specialized upstream error contracts remain open.
Real R exit-code retention, persistent preservation markers and stderr relay pass on Windows and Linux. Exact upstream merged-log filenames remain different.

Six checks passed with a root gateway and an unprivileged log writer: ownership, permissions, bounded rotation and exit-code retention. All log operations run under worker credentials; NFS itself remains untested.
allow, deny, sameorigin and legacy allow-from are implemented; response headers and inheritance have live HTTP checks. ALLOW-FROM remains obsolete in modern browsers.

cases.progress: XHR streaming, eventsource and htmlfile passed real Shiny browser tests; obsolete IE transports remain unverified.

cases.progress: XHR, iframe XHR and JSONP passed real Shiny browser tests; obsolete IE/XDR remains unverified.

cases.description: Session IDs, heartbeats, disconnect deadlines, origin/iframe behavior
Shiny Server reconnect, worker affinity and expired-session behavior
cases.progress: Nine candidate recovery checks pass; six wire cases also pass on upstream. Large-message input/output and 3 MiB replay pass. Configurable limits and UTF-8 client buffer accounting replace previous hard limits. Exhaustive failure equivalence remains open.

cases.description: URL and server bookmark storage, restoration and isolation
cases.progress: Server-side bookmarks survive R worker replacement. Posit Shiny Server 1.5.23.1030 and ShinyHarbor restore each other's numeric-input bookmarks using the same Unix app path/account/store. Custom callbacks, uploaded-file state and arbitrary existing stores remain under review.

cases.description: session$request, session$clientData, identity and environment contract
cases.progress: Hosted-runtime metadata identifies ShinyHarbor before app evaluation. Unix Bash profiles, supervisor credentials, R environment selection and r_path precedence pass. Basic/proxy session identity and worker authentication pass. Complete environment parity remains under review.

cases.description: Scheduling, spawn failures, idle termination, crash behavior and limits
restart.txt and per-app overrides without disturbing unrelated apps
cases.progress: restart.txt generation draining and browser bookmark restoration passed; opt-in app overrides are parsed and tracked.

cases.description: SIGHUP/config reload, draining, process trees and termination behavior
cases.progress: Atomic application reloads passed seven Windows browser/CLI cases and two Linux SIGHUP cases. Listener/TLS/global changes still require restart.

cases.description: Interactive R Markdown discovery, launch behavior and resources
cases.progress: Three real browser routes passed reactive R Markdown and relative-resource checks with rmarkdown 2.32 and Pandoc 3.12.1; comprehensive document semantics remain open.

cases.description: htmlwidgets, shared dependencies, UI updates and custom messages
Sanitization, templates, error status and full-stacktrace controls
Paths, formats, retention, user ownership and access log behavior
Professional-equivalent authentication, identity, authorization and session isolation
cases.progress: Trusted proxy SSO and inherited user/group policies passed ten real R/browser and denial cases, including local overrides and reconnect identity changes. Native PAM/LDAP/OIDC and licensed professional comparison remain open.

cases.description: Multiple workers, utilization, queue bounds and overload/recovery
cases.progress: Load-factor scaling, worker ceiling, overload recovery and idle-session limits passed seven real R tests. Licensed professional scheduling equivalence remains unverified.

cases.description: Documented accurate monitoring and failure reporting
Staging/production issuance, challenge handling, persistence, renewal and failure recovery
Unauthorized access, traversal, resource exhaustion and secrets exposure
Real application integration with the moving latest stable CRAN Shiny
cases.progress: Real Shiny 1.14.0 runs the browser/transport suites. Hosted runtime metadata identifies ShinyHarbor before application evaluation. Continuously testing later package releases and full conformance remain open.
